subject: Dedicated capacity RFI: GPU family prioritization & throughput harmonization
messages:
From: Maya Rao <maya@opslyft.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: Dedicated capacity sizing + GPU family guidance

Hi Vivek —

OpsLyft is kicking off an evaluation of Redwood Dedicated for a production generative feature set and we need a short RFI to inform our procurement and sizing workstreams. High level asks:

- Recommendations for GPU families and a phased reservation plan (pilot -> committed).
- Throughput targets we should plan for given our traffic profile (see bullets below).
- Any recommended quantization / model variants to reduce cost with minimal quality impact.

Quick context:
- Peak request rate target: ~250 req/s (peak, bursty).
- Day average: ~10M tokens/day.
- Typical sequence length: ~512 tokens (prompt + gen).
- Models: primary is Mistral-7B-fast for routine queries; a minority set (~20%) will hit Llama2-70B for higher-fidelity completions.
- Region: US (multi-AZ preferred).

Procurement timeline: looking to decide vendor and reservation approach by end of June; pilot could start July. Attaching our RFI template for your convenience.

Attachment: opslyft-rfi-template.pdf (application/pdf)

Could you confirm availability for a 30-minute tech sync this week?

Thanks,
Maya Rao
Product & Platform Lead
OpsLyft

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Maya Rao <maya@opslyft.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: Dedicated capacity sizing + GPU family guidance

Hi Maya —

Thanks for the clear brief and the RFI. We can definitely support a phased reservation approach that balances cost and tail-latency risk. A few quick clarifying questions before we lock numbers:

1) At peak 250 req/s, what's the concurrency distribution? (average inflight requests; p95/p99 concurrency)
2) Target tail latency SLO for the 70B path (p95/p99 target in ms)?
3) Percent of requests that hit the 70B model during peak windows — you mention ~20% overall, does that spike higher at certain times?

Preliminary guidance (very high level):
- For the 70B workload we recommend planning for H100-class instances (or A100-80GB depending on availability) with Q4/INT8 quantization if you can accept a small eval runway — quantized 70B can cut per-token cost by ~2–3x versus FP16 and typically sustains higher packing.
- For the 7B production path, an A100 or 4-bit-quantized Vram-light instance should be more than adequate and will be much cheaper to reserve at scale.

To move fast I attached a one-page worksheet that Ben and I will use to map your traffic into a phased reservation: pilot (capacity for 20% of forecasted peak, validate tail with synthetic load), then committed runrate (reserve for 70–80% of expected steady peak) with burst lane for short spikes.

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-sku-recommendation.xlsx (spreadsheet)

I can do a 30-minute sync today at 3pm PT or tomorrow at 10am PT — what works best?

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Maya Rao <maya@opslyft.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, procurement@opslyft.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: Dedicated capacity sizing + GPU family guidance

Thanks Vivek —

Answers inline:
- Concurrency: average 40 concurrent, p95 ~120, p99 ~220 during peak 10–15 minute spikes.
- Tail latency SLO: p95 <= 300ms for 7B; p95 <= 1s for 70B. p99 targets are softer but we want to understand tail risk.
- 70B usage: baseline 20% overall but can spike to ~35% during morning batch/analytics windows.

I've dropped our internal traffic metrics (CSV) in our shared folder and attached a trimmed export for the RFI. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0BzOpsLyftShared/metrics

Attachment: opslyft-internal-traffic-metrics.csv (text/csv)

We can take the 3pm PT slot today for the sync.

—Maya
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Maya Rao <maya@opslyft.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: Dedicated capacity sizing + GPU family guidance

Thanks for the metrics, Maya — ran a quick mapping against Redwood throughput models and here are pragmatic recommendations for a pilot -> committed reservation plan. Notes and assumptions are at the top; numbers are conservative to preserve tail SLOs.

Assumptions:
- 70B (quantized Q4_8bit) sustained inference throughput: ~20–30 req/s per H100 (depends on packing and KV cache reuse).
- 7B (int4 quantized) sustained: ~120–160 req/s per A100-class GPU or equivalent packed instance.
- Avg sequence 512 tokens used in costing; if average falls below 300 tokens your effective req/s per GPU increases.

Recommendation (phased):
1) Pilot (month 1): 4 x H100 (for 70B pilot capacity) + 8 x A100-equivalent (for 7B). Pilot config covers ~20–25% of forecasted peak and lets us validate p99 tail with realistic traffic.
2) Ramp (month 2–3): increase to 8 x H100 + 16 x A100-equivalent as committed baseline.
3) Steady-state reservation (month 4+): 12 x H100 + 24 x A100-equivalent committed with an automated burst lane that can spin additional ephemeral H100 capacity for short spikes (billing for burst usage until fully committed).

Operational controls and mitigations:
- Autoscaling/burst lane: keep a burst pool (shared across AZs) and a circuit-breaker that routes to smaller models if tail latency exceeds thresholds.
- Model pinning & fallback: pin the 70B revision you validate during pilot; fallback to 7B or a distilled 13B in extreme tail conditions.
- Quantization: start pilot with Q4/INT8 for 70B; run a small eval set to measure quality delta. If acceptable, roll to committed to cut cost ~2x relative to FP16.

Estimated per-GPU throughput (guide):
- H100 (70B, Q4): 25 req/s avg -> with 12 H100 committed that covers ~300 req/s sustained for 70B path if well packed; knob: pack prompt windows and use KV caching aggressively.
- A100-eq (7B, int4): 140 req/s avg -> with 24 units you get ~3.3k req/s capacity for the 7B path.

Next steps:
- Vivek/Laura to produce a short SOW and reservation estimate (line-itemed by SKU and month); include a DocuSign link for SOW acceptance.
- OpsLyft to run the small eval set against quantized 70B (we can provide evaluation harness).

I'm attaching the workbook with the capacity math and a couple of scenario tabs (conservative / optimistic). We can refine after the sync.

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-sku-recommendation.xlsx (spreadsheet)

—Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
